title: Thousands of Migrants Remain on Ceuta's Streets as Madrid Voices Confidence in Morocco's EU Commitment
detail: Weeks after the Poniente port camp opened with only 1,700 places, thousands of migrants remained on Ceuta's streets and beaches, with La Moncloa citing roughly 3,000 still outside official facilities while the Ceuta city government maintains a considerably higher figure. Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska again described Morocco as a 'socio leal' (loyal partner) for its containment efforts, and PM Pedro Sánchez reiterated there is no solid evidence that Rabat's government orchestrated the July 30-31 crossings. Spanish government sources said they are confident Morocco will honour the commitment it communicated to the EU on Sep 14 to readmit migrants, including Moroccan nationals and unaccompanied minors.

title: Ceuta Rejects Becoming Permanent 'Macrocentro' for Migrants, Warns of Pull-Factor Effect
detail: Alfonso Conejo, Ceuta's director general of Governance, rejected the Spanish government's plan to build two EU-funded Temporary Attention Centers for Foreigners (CATE) in the city, saying 'Ceuta is Spain and a Spanish city cannot become a macrocentro de estancia temporal' and warning that permanent large-scale reception facilities would not be viable and would produce a kind of 'efecto llamada' (pull effect) attracting more migrants rather than deterring them. Conejo instead demanded a serious EU-level return policy, modern 21st-century border infrastructure, and faster deployment of state resources including Civil Guard and administrative personnel. More than 72,000 people entered Ceuta from Morocco in the July 30-31 crossing, and the city has not recovered normalcy nearly two months on.
